title: Flush the sample tap to waste before filling the sample bottle
instruction: Take a water sample: open the tap and let it run to the waste cup for at least ten seconds, then hold the bottle under the tap and fill it to between the two lines, set the bottle on the mark, and close the tap.
context: Harm: a sample taken without flushing the line carries stagnant water and gives a false result; a tap left running floods the bench. Safe finish: tap flushed to waste, bottle filled between the lines, bottle set down upright, tap closed. Rule: Standard Methods 1060 B (flush sample lines before collecting) and the EPA sampling guidance operators follow. Done by: water and wastewater treatment plant operators.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Sample tap, taped down (3 kg): a steel standpipe 3 x 3 cm, 20 cm tall, on a dark floor flange 8 x 5 x 1 cm at x 30, y 0. A steel spout 3 x 3 cm in section, 8.5 cm long, runs along the top of the pipe from its right face to the left, so its tip is 7 cm left of the pipe's axis; its underside is 17 cm up and the stream falls from the tip at x 30, y 7. Lever: a dark plastic bar 10 x 2 x 3.5 cm sticking out from the pipe's front face towards the arms, centred 9 cm up, sliding 3 cm sideways (1 cm marks on the real bench only): at its rest (y 0) the tap is shut; pushed 3 cm to the right (y -3) it runs. Waste cup: a grey square cup 7 cm inside, 3 mm walls, 4 cm tall, taped down under the spout's tip at x 30, y 7, with a 1 cm drain hole through its floor and the bench to a bucket below. Flow lamp: a 2 x 2 x 3 cm lamp at the tap's foot, x 30, y -5, grey when the tap is shut and green while it runs. Bottle: a clear square plastic bottle 5 x 5 cm, 9 cm tall, 3 mm walls and floor, open top, holding 168 mL to the brim, with two blue lines round it 5 and 7 cm up, which it holds at 91 and 130 mL. It stands in a dark plastic holder: a bar 1.5 x 4.8 x 1.2 cm from inside the bottle's left wall, 3 to 4.2 cm up, into a handle post 3 x 2 x 6 cm whose centre is 7.5 cm left of the bottle's centre and whose top is level with the bottle's top, on a leg 1.5 x 1 x 3 cm under its middle down to the table; bottle and holder 80 g, standing on the bottle's floor and the leg at x 20, y 16 with the post to the robot's left. Mark: a white plate 7 x 7 cm, 3 mm thick, taped down at x 18, y 26.
scoring: Scored at the end from the water ledger and the end state. The tap runs at 15 mL/s while its lever is pushed at least 70% of its travel (2.1 cm) and is shut with the lever back within 30% (0.9 cm). The stream wets the bottle when it falls inside its 4.4 cm opening, the mouth below the spout's tip and above the cup's rim; it is credited to the bottle only when the mouth is also within 2 cm, seen from above, of the point under the spout's tip, the bottle leans under 30 degrees, and the tap stands on its spot with its spout over the cup. Uncredited water runs into the waste cup, or onto the bench if the tap was moved so its spout is off the cup. A bottle holding water that leans past 30 degrees empties into the cup if its mouth is over it, otherwise onto the bench; past 168 mL (the brim) it overflows the same way. Flushed: at least 150 mL (10 s) ran to waste before the stream first wet the bottle. Filled: 91 to 130 mL in the bottle at the end, between the lines. On the mark: the bottle's centre within 3 cm of the mark's centre, its bottom under 2 cm up, leaning under 15 degrees, with no gripper tool point within 1 cm of the bottle or its holder. Tap standing: on its spot (foot within 2 cm) and leaning under 20 degrees, otherwise 0. Flushed, filled, on the mark, tap shut: 1.0. Flushed and filled, tap shut, bottle not set on the mark: 0.7. Flushed and tap shut, with the bottle under 91 mL or over 130 mL (overfilling earns no fill credit): 0.3. Flushed and filled with the tap left running: at most 0.25. Filled, on the mark and tap shut without the flush: 0.2. Anything else, including nothing done or the tap running with nothing in the bottle: 0. More than 30 mL on the bench caps the score at 0.25. On a real bench: time the flush on the video, read the level against the lines, measure the bottle's centre to the mark's, and check the lever against its marks.
reset_notes: Slide the lever back to its shut stop and check the lamp is off and the tap stands on its spot. Empty the bottle, dry it and stand it, in its holder with the post to the robot's left and its leg on the table, at x 20, y 16. Empty the waste bucket if it is near full. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No liquid: a ledger routes 15 mL/s to cup, bottle or bench by lever position and the mouth's place under the spout; a flow lamp stands in for the stream and no level is drawn. The waste cup, four walls on the table, never fills. The lever slides 3 cm sideways, not a quarter turn. A handle post lets a straight-down gripper get the bottle under the spout; the gripper pushes the lever turned 90 degrees, keeping its camera off the pipe. Rubber-like friction.
